# Loading in the cleaned and split data
```{r}
madness_train <- readRDS("training_data.rds")
madness_test <- readRDS("testing_data.rds")
all_games <- readRDS("clean_data_full.rds")
```


# Simple logistic model
Starting off, I will make a simple logistic logistic model that includes all of the features in prediction.
```{r}
#Creating a simple logistic model to predict churn from the training data
simple_log_model <- glm(winner ~ ., data = madness_train, family = binomial)

#Looking at what is significant, and the relative weights. This will guide decision making when creating a larger model
summary(simple_log_model)

#Predicting the test data based on the model
madness_prob_simple <- predict(simple_log_model, madness_test, type = "response")
madness_pred_simple <- ifelse(madness_prob_simple >= 0.5, "1", "0")

# Creating a confusion matrix to compare the test predictions to actual results
library(caret)
confusionMatrix(as.factor(madness_pred_simple), as.factor(madness_test$winner), positive = "1")

```


# Creating correlation matrix to guide optimization
Now I will explore how the data are correlated to see what interactions may improve our logistic model. The correlation plot will be evaluated using the entire data-set. 
```{r}
# Correlations among all dummy-coded features
correlations <- cor(all_games, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")


library(corrplot)

#Create a correlation plot
corrplot(
  correlations,
  method = "color",
  type = "upper",
  tl.cex = 0.2,
  tl.srt = 45,
  mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0)
)

# Due to number of oclumns maybe correlation plot hard to read- print out interactions that have a high correlation
correlation_table <- as.data.frame(as.table(correlations))
names(correlation_table) <- c("Feature_1", "Feature_2", "Correlation")

# Keep each pair once, exclude self-correlations, and filter by threshold
correlation_table <- subset(
  correlation_table,
  as.character(Feature_1) < as.character(Feature_2) &
    (Correlation < -0.8 | Correlation > 0.8)
)

# Sort strongest correlations first
correlation_table <- correlation_table[
  order(-abs(correlation_table$Correlation)),
]

print(correlation_table, row.names = FALSE)
```
# Reverse step-wise model to optimize included parameters 
```{r}
big_logmodel <- glm(
  winner ~ . +
    # Seed and team strength
    I(seed.2 - seed.1) * I(srs.1 - srs.2) +
    I(seed.2 - seed.1) * I(win_pct.1 - win_pct.2) +
    I(srs.1 - srs.2) * I(sos.1 - sos.2) +

    # Shooting and scoring
    I(efg_pct.1 - efg_pct.2) * I(fg3a_per_fga_pct.1 - fg3a_per_fga_pct.2) +
    I(efg_pct.1 - efg_pct.2) * I(ft_rate.1 - ft_rate.2) +
    I(fg_pct.1 - fg_pct.2) * I(pts_pg.1 - pts_pg.2) +

    # Ball handling and defense
    I(tov_pct.2 - tov_pct.1) * I(ast_pct.1 - ast_pct.2) +
    I(blk_pct.1 - blk_pct.2) * I(fg_pct_opp.2 - fg_pct_opp.1) +
    I(stl_pg.1 - stl_pg.2) * I(tov_pct.2 - tov_pct.1) +

    # Rebounding and opponent stats
    I(trb_pct.1 - trb_pct.2) * I(trb_pg_opp.2 - trb_pg_opp.1) +
    I(pts_pg_opp.2 - pts_pg_opp.1) * I(fg_pct_opp.2 - fg_pct_opp.1) +

    # Experience and bench contributions
    I(exp_avg.1 - exp_avg.2) * I(height_avg.1 - height_avg.2) +
    I(mp_bench_pct.1 - mp_bench_pct.2) * I(pts_bench_pct.1 - pts_bench_pct.2) +

    # Nonlinear effects
    I((seed.2 - seed.1)^2) +
    I((srs.1 - srs.2)^2) +
    I((efg_pct.1 - efg_pct.2)^2) +
    I((tov_pct.2 - tov_pct.1)^2),
  data = madness_train,
  family = binomial
)


finalLog <- step(big_logmodel, direction = "backward", trace = 0)
summary(finalLog)
```

```{r}
madness_prob_stacked <- predict(finalLog, newdata = madness_test, type = "response")
madness_pred_finalLog <- ifelse(madness_prob_stacked >= 0.5, 1, 0)

# Evaluate predictions
logConfusionMatrix <- confusionMatrix(
  as.factor(madness_pred_finalLog),
  as.factor(madness_test$winner),
  positive = "1")

logConfusionMatrix
```

```{r}
saveRDS(logConfusionMatrix, "logistic_confusion_v2.rds")
saveRDS(madness_prob_stacked, "logistic_stacked_prob_v2.rds")
```
